::: {.callout-warning}
This fit is historical evidence behind the exploratory bundle values. It is
retained for provenance and diagnosis, not as an accepted ionic parameter set.
Its numbers come from the historical ePC-SAFT 1.5.2 runtime and are not
regenerated on the greenfield Engine; current per-species scores for the
adopted record are in the [overview](../notebook.qmd#speciation).
:::

# Question

Could a small set of MEAH⁺ and MEACOO⁻ segment, dispersion, Born and mutual
interaction parameters improve the available MEA speciation data while
remaining numerically and scientifically interpretable?

# Starting point and strategy

Eight nominally 30 mass% MEA states at ambient pressure supplied 22 species
residuals. The states came from Böttinger 2008 (four), Jakobsen, Krane &
Svendsen 2005 (two), and Matin et al. 2012 (two), covering MEAH⁺, carbamate,
bicarbonate, carbonate and combined free/protonated MEA observations.

The historical ePC-SAFT 1.5.2 runtime was used. A bounded soft-L1 least-squares
fit used log₁₀(model/data) residuals, scaled parameter coordinates and a weak
pull toward the starting vector. Seven coordinates moved simultaneously:

::: {.parameter-table .parameter-change-table}
| Parameter | Starting value → retained value |
|:--|:--|
| MEAH⁺ $\sigma$ (Å) | 3.563 → 3.48508556586 |
| MEAH⁺ $\epsilon/k$ (K) | 228.71 → 232.687201645 |
| MEAH⁺ $d_B$ (Å) | 3.563 → 3.53322927146 |
| MEACOO⁻ $\sigma$ (Å) | 3.5605 → 3.53543525721 |
| MEACOO⁻ $\epsilon/k$ (K) | 533.11 → 453.265244384 |
| MEACOO⁻ $d_B$ (Å) | 3.5605 → 3.54107030822 |
| MEAH⁺–MEACOO⁻ $k_{ij}$ | 0 → −0.00201813457644 |
:::

# Numerical result

Overall log-RMSE changed from **0.27144 to 0.26766** (about 1.4%). Mean
absolute log residual changed 0.17390 → 0.17025 and median absolute log
residual changed 0.10105 → 0.09885. Carbamate RMSE improved 0.09008 →
0.08282, while combined MEA + MEAH⁺ slightly worsened 0.10685 → 0.10976.

Two final residual rows at the Böttinger 20 °C, loading 0.075 state came from
a nonconverged solve. Best-effort finite predictions remained in the reported
metrics. The fit was speciation-only: pressure parity was not regenerated, no
independent validation was run, and no confidence interval was established.

# Conclusion and limits

The fit records a small in-sample improvement, but the improvement is too
small and too entangled with failed-state predictions to qualify the seven
coordinates. The retained values are useful historical seeds and a warning
about the identification problem: speciation alone did not demonstrate that
MEA ion size, dispersion, Born diameter and mutual interaction can be
separately estimated. The later volumetric and coupled-fit plans therefore
kept these roles explicit rather than treating this fit as a solved ionic
regression.
